title: Human Vision Has Quirks That AI Can’t Match - Nautilus
gist: Human vision's imperfections such as blind spots, after-images and susceptibility to optical illusions may be adaptive features, while AI vision systems excel at accurate spatial mapping but cannot reproduce how human perception alters an image.

insights.claim: Human vision does not represent the world exactly as it is, exhibiting blind spots, after-images and susceptibility to optical illusions.
insights.speaker: Kristen French
insights.so_what: Frames the perceptual gap between people and machine vision systems.
insights.quote: Our eyes do not always represent the world exactly as it is. We have blind spots. We see after-images. We are tricked by optical illusions.

insights.claim: Some imperfections of human vision may be adaptive features of biological vision rather than flaws.
insights.speaker: Kristen French
insights.so_what: Suggests that copying human perceptual 'bugs' could be a design direction for more human-like machine perception.
insights.quote: But some of these imperfections may be adaptive features of biological vision rather than flaws.

insights.claim: Current AI vision systems are very good at accurately mapping objects in physical space but cannot reproduce the ways human visual experience alters what is seen.
insights.speaker: Kristen French
insights.so_what: Highlights a remaining gap for robotics and AI systems meant to perceive the world the way humans do.
insights.quote: They are very good at accurately mapping an object in physical space, but they can’t reproduce the ways that picture might be altered by the human visual experience.
insights.locator: Today’s AI vision systems are imperfect
